verses.text: Now the snake was more cunning than any of the wild animals the LORD God had made. It said to the woman, "Did God really say, 'You must not eat from any tree in the garden'?"
The woman answered the snake, "We may eat fruit from the trees in the garden.
But about the tree in the middle of the garden, God said, 'You must not eat its fruit. Do not even touch it, or you will die.'"
"You will not die!" the snake said to the woman.
"God knows that when you eat from it, your eyes will be opened. You will be like God, knowing good and evil."

The woman saw that the fruit of the tree was good for food and lovely to look at, and that it was desirable because it could make a person wise. So she took some of the fruit and ate it. She also gave some to her husband, who was with her, and he ate it.
Then the eyes of both of them were opened, and they realised that they were naked. So they sewed fig leaves together and made coverings for themselves.
In the cool part of the day, they heard the sound of the LORD God walking in the garden. The man and his wife hid from the LORD God among the trees of the garden.
But the LORD God called out to the man, "Where are you?"
He answered, "I heard you in the garden, and I was afraid because I was naked. So I hid."
God asked, "Who told you that you were naked? Have you eaten from the tree that I commanded you not to eat from?"
The man said, "The woman you put here with me gave me fruit from the tree, and I ate it."
Then the LORD God said to the woman, "What is this that you have done?" The woman said, "The snake tricked me, and I ate."

So the LORD God said to the snake, "Because you have done this, you are cursed more than all the farm animals and all the wild animals. You will crawl on your belly, and you will eat dust all the days of your life.
I will make you and the woman enemies of each other, and your offspring and her offspring will be enemies too. He will crush your head, and you will strike his heel."
To the woman he said, "I will greatly increase your pain when you carry children. In pain you will give birth. You will long for your husband, and he will rule over you."

To Adam he said, "You listened to your wife and ate fruit from the tree that I commanded you not to eat from. So the ground is cursed because of you. All the days of your life you will have to work hard to get food from it.
It will grow thorns and weeds for you, and you will eat the plants of the field.
You will sweat to earn your bread until you go back to the ground, because you were taken from it. You are dust, and to dust you will return."
Adam named his wife Eve, because she would become the mother of all who live.
The LORD God made clothes from animal skins for Adam and his wife, and he dressed them.

Then the LORD God said, "Look, the man has become like one of us, knowing good and evil. He must not be allowed to reach out his hand, take fruit from the tree of life as well, eat it and live for ever."
So the LORD God sent him out of the Garden of Eden to work the ground from which he had been taken.

After he drove the man out, he placed cherubim, mighty heavenly beings, on the east side of the Garden of Eden. He also placed a flaming sword there that flashed back and forth, to guard the way to the tree of life.
